beats.beat: The company sells specialty chemicals across four categories: functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals, and hard minerals. These are used in a wide range of industries such as paints, plastics, cosmetics, and construction.
Revenues are not dependent on any single customer, but the top 10 customers collectively accounted for about 59% of revenue in each of the last three fiscal years (2015–2017).
The company exports to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Sri Lanka; total exports over the past five years amounted to ₹1,068.18 lakh.

A key structural feature is the long-term arrangement with corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited, through which the company markets and sells its products. This means the company's distribution depends heavily on a related party.

business.heading: What the company does

beats.beat: The company has reported financials for six periods: FY2013, FY2014, FY2015, FY2016, FY2017, and the six months ended Sep 2017. All figures in ₹ lakh as per the filing (to be converted to ₹ crore in the final report).

Profit after tax: The company moved from a loss of ₹27.40 lakh in FY2013 and ₹12.17 lakh in FY2014 to profit of ₹149.58 lakh in FY2015, ₹90.18 lakh in FY2016, ₹174.82 lakh in FY2017, and ₹132.75 lakh in first half of FY2018.

Net cash from operations has been erratic: ₹200.97 lakh in FY2013, ₹127.73 lakh in FY2014, ₹422.36 lakh in FY2015, a strong ₹802.59 lakh in FY2016, then a sharp negative ₹349.75 lakh in FY2017, and positive ₹124.86 lakh in H1 FY2018.
Total assets have grown from ₹3,018.66 lakh in FY2013 to ₹3,424.96 lakh in Sep 2017, with a dip in FY2015–FY2016.
Basic earnings per share (in ₹ per share of face value ₹10): –0.45 in FY2013, –0.20 in FY2014, 2.47 in FY2015, 1.46 in FY2016, 2.43 in FY2017, and 1.48 for H1 FY2018.

financials.heading: Financial performance
financials.purpose: Present revenue, PAT, cash flows, and key ratios for all reported periods (FY2013 to Sep 2017), converting to ₹ crore. Highlight the turnaround from losses to profits and the volatile operating cash flows.

beats.beat: Promoters are Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh, Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh, and 20 Microns Limited. They collectively hold 89,48,270 equity shares, representing 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity share capital.
Promoter group members (excluding promoters) hold 21,510 shares, or 0.24% of pre-issue capital. This means promoters and promoter group together own 100% of the company before the IPO.
The authorised share capital is ₹2,000 lakh (20,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 each) and the issued, subscribed, and paid-up capital as of Sep 30, 2017, is ₹897 lakh (89,70,000 shares).
The company has engaged in related-party transactions with its promoter group in all reported periods. These transactions are disclosed in the financial statements.

Governance flags include: (i) contingent liabilities of ₹29.11 lakh as of Sep 2017, (ii) negative operating cash flows in FY2017, (iii) some instances of non-filing/delays with ROC, and (iv) lack of statutory licenses for one manufacturing facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia.

beats.beat: The Indian specialty chemicals market was estimated at about ₹1,000 billion in fiscal 2017 and grew at 10–12% CAGR from 2014 to 2017. CRISIL Research expects it to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward.
The industry is highly fragmented, with small and medium enterprises holding 70–75% market share. Only a few Indian players have the scale to compete with global giants on product development.
Growth drivers include rising GDP and consumption, increasing urbanisation, and government initiatives such as the Draft National Chemical Policy and 100% FDI allowance in the sector.

Regulatory factors include the implementation of GST from July 1, 2017, REACH compliance for exports to Europe, and the establishment of Petroleum, Chemicals and Petrochemicals Investment Regions (PCPIRs) with proposed investments of about ₹9 trillion.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals Limited processes and sells specialty chemicals, primarily functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals, and hard minerals. It has a long-term arrangement with its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, to market and sell its products through the promoter's network.
The company is bringing an initial public offering to list on NSE EMERGE, the SME platform. The lead manager is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who 20 Microns Nano Minerals is, what it does, its corporate promoter relationship, and that it is raising capital via an SME IPO.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of equity shares (no offer for sale in the disclosed extracts). The proceeds will be used to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, Gujarat. General corporate purposes and listing on NSE EMERGE are also stated objects.
The lead manager to the issue is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited, and the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

offer.heading: The IPO offer
offer.purpose: Explain the offer structure: fresh issue (presumed), objects of the issue, lead manager, registrar, and listing platform.

beats.beat: No long-term customer or supplier agreements: The company operates entirely on purchase orders. The absence of contracts means revenue and raw-material costs are subject to abrupt changes.
Negative operating cash flow in FY2017: The company reported a net cash outflow of ₹349.75 lakh from operations in the most recent full fiscal year, indicating potential cash flow stress.
Missing statutory licenses for one manufacturing unit: The company has not obtained certain required licenses for its facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia, and could face penalties or shutdown.
Contingent liabilities: As of Sep 30, 2017, contingent liabilities aggregate ₹29.11 lakh. If any materialise, they could affect profitability.
Intense competition and pricing pressure: The specialty chemicals industry is highly fragmented and competitive. Pricing pressures could erode margins and reduce revenues.
